interest: This document provides a concise administrative record of pre-World War II U.S. government monitoring of Japanese military personnel stationed in the United States under the rubric of language study. It highlights the inter-agency coordination between the State Department and the Department of Justice in verifying diplomatic status and tracking the activities of Japanese naval officers attached to the Naval Attaché's Office in Washington during the tense months leading up to late 1941.
overview: This file consists of a State Department 'List of Papers' docket sheet (File No. 894.3211) cataloguing correspondence from late 1940 through September 1941 concerning the detail of Japanese naval officer Masakazu (Masakusu) Tukasaki to the United States. The recorded documents track communications from the Japanese Embassy providing his biographical profile and correcting his rank from Engineer Lieutenant to Ordnance Lieutenant, alongside inquiries and investigative reports from the Department of Justice regarding his diplomatic status and surveillance of his activities as a language officer attached to the Japanese Naval Attaché's Office in Washington.

subfiles.about: A State Department docket sheet listing correspondence regarding the assignment and surveillance of Japanese naval language officer Masakazu Tukasaki in the United States.
subfiles.summary: This docket sheet indexes four incoming and outgoing communications dated between October 17 [1940] and September 10, 1941, regarding Japanese naval officer Masakazu (Masakusu) Tukasaki. Initial entries from the Japanese Embassy transmit his biographical record as an Engineer Lieutenant and promptly correct his designation to Ordnance Lieutenant. Subsequent entries record communications with the Department of Justice inquiring into his diplomatic status and transmitting background information and intelligence reports concerning his recent activities as a language officer attached to the Japanese Naval Attaché's Office in Washington.
